headline: Highest risk is capability conflict and cascading error: Devin’s broad write/network/OAuth powers can act on any content it ingests, while awesome-python is non-runnable and contributes no protective controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable or I/O surfaces, so it cannot inject directly. B can ingest files, MCP, and browser content, so if an operator manually copies content from A’s docs or repo into B, prompt injection is possible but requires unusual bridging. The pair lacks a default shared channel.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-derived text into B’s chat or files
IF B parses copied content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces
Do not paste A content into B prompts
Add a provenance banner before any copied text
Use read-only exports for A-derived material

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, while B can read files and send data to external integrations. Leakage from A into B is limited because A is a static collection and not a data processor, but B can still expose any manually transferred sensitive content through its broad network and integration surfaces.
conditions: IF sensitive material is manually placed into B’s cloud workspace files
IF B forwards those files through GitHub, Slack, Jira, Notion, or MCP integrations
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in B’s workspace
Restrict B integrations to least privilege
Use redacted test data only
Review outbound sync destinations before use

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capability, but B has unrestricted filesystem, git, and network write paths in a shared-session cloud workspace. The conflict is one-sided rather than symmetric, yet B can still overwrite or mutate shared artifacts if A is used as a source of instructions or file lists. Uncertainty about A’s non-runnable status does not reduce B’s write risk.
conditions: IF B operates on a repo or workspace also referenced by A-derived instructions
IF multiple B sessions touch the same GitHub PR or shared integration thread
mitigations: Assign one writer per repo branch
Use branch protection and PR reviews
Pause parallel B sessions on shared artifacts
Lock shared files before edits

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a static collection, not an executor, but B’s autonomous planner-executor model can treat imported content as authoritative and then act through shell, git, or integrations. If A-derived guidance is wrong or stale, B can propagate it into commits, tickets, or messages without a verification step. The interaction is plausible in default B workflows once content is copied over.
conditions: IF A-derived text is used as an input source for B
IF B is allowed to commit, message, or ticket based on that text without human review
mitigations: Require human verification before B acts
Mark A content as non-authoritative
Add a checklist for source validation
Disable auto-send on B for critical actions

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source and non-runnable, so it raises no residency issue by itself. B is closed-source, cloud-hosted, and handles source code, issue trackers, chat, and secrets through third-party integrations; that creates a compliance surface for retention and residency mismatches if regulated data is introduced. The other agent is not cited as a compliance source because it does not process such data.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B’s workspace or integrations
IF B’s retention or residency settings differ from the organization’s policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B
Review retention settings in connected tools
Limit B to non-sensitive repos
Document approved data classes for B
